success=True data={'content': '     1	KVP — Key-Value Protocol Specification
     2	======================================
     3	
     4	1. Introduction
     5	
     6	   KVP is a simple text-based protocol for an in-memory key-value store.
     7	   Commands are line-oriented. Each command is a single line of text.
     8	   Responses follow a structured format described below.
     9	
    10	2. Commands
    11	
    12	   2.1 SET <key> <value>
    13	       Store the given value under the given key.
    14	       Response: OK
    15	       Errors: ERR key_too_long (if key exceeds 64 chars)
    16	               ERR value_too_large (if value exceeds 1024 chars)
    17	               ERR store_full (if store has 100 keys and key is new)
    18	
    19	   2.2 GET <key>
    20	       Retrieve the value stored under the given key.
    21	       Response: the value on a single line
    22	       Errors: ERR key_not_found
    23	
    24	   2.3 DEL <key>
    25	       Remove the given key from the store.
    26	       Response: OK
    27	       Errors: ERR key_not_found
    28	
    29	   2.4 KEYS
    30	       List all stored keys.
    31	       Response: one key per line, terminated by END
    32	
    33	   2.5 COUNT
    34	       Return the number of stored keys.
    35	       Response: COUNT <n>
    36	
    37	   2.6 EXISTS <key>
    38	       Check if a key exists.
    39	       Response: TRUE or FALSE
    40	
    41	   2.7 FLUSH
    42	       Remove all keys.
    43	       Response: OK
    44	
    45	   2.8 MSET <key1> <value1> <key2> <value2> ...
    46	       Set multiple key-value pairs atomically.
    47	       Response: OK <n> (where n = number of pairs set)
    48	
    49	   2.9 MGET <key1> <key2> ...
    50	       Get multiple values.
    51	       Response: value or NIL per key, one per line, terminated by END
    52	
    53	   2.10 SETEX <key> <seconds> <value>
    54	        Set a key with an expiration time in seconds.
    55	        Response: OK
    56	        After expiration, the key is treated as non-existent.
    57	
    58	   2.11 TTL <key>
    59	        Return remaining time-to-live in seconds, or -1 if no expiry.
    60	        Errors: ERR key_not_found
    61	
    62	   2.12 APPEND <key> <value>
    63	        Append to existing value, or create new key.
    64	        Response: OK <new_length>
    65	
    66	   2.13 RENAME <old_key> <new_key>
    67	        Rename a key.
    68	        Response: OK
    69	        Errors: ERR key_not_found
    70	
    71	   2.14 TYPE <key>
    72	        Return the type of the value (STRING or INTEGER).
    73	        Errors: ERR key_not_found
    74	
    75	   2.15 DUMP
    76	        Return all key-value pairs as <key>=<value>, terminated by END
    77	
    78	3. Limits
    79	
    80	   Maximum key length: 64 characters
    81	   Maximum value size: 1024 characters
    82	   Maximum stored keys: 100
    83	
    84	4. Error Codes
    85	
    86	   ERR key_not_found    — key does not exist
    87	   ERR key_too_long     — key exceeds maximum length
    88	   ERR value_too_large  — value exceeds maximum size
    89	   ERR store_full       — store at maximum capacity for new keys
    90	   ERR unknown_command  — unrecognized command
    91	
    92	5. Response Format
    93	
    94	   Success: OK, OK <detail>, TRUE, FALSE, COUNT <n>
    95	   Value: the raw value on its own line
    96	   List: one item per line, terminated by END
    97	   Error: ERR <error_code>', 'file_path': '/srv/jwteam_clone/shared/run_current/workspace/protocol_spec.txt', 'line_count': 97} error=None
